companyIntro.culture: Evidence over opinion. A result is not a result until someone else can reproduce it.

projectBackground.name: Invoice Processing Automation
projectBackground.context: Finance keys 800 supplier invoices a month. The CFO wants to know whether automation pays back and what happens when it fails.

manager.name: Eva Jansen
manager.note: Automate boring and repeatable work, and design the failure path before the happy path.

assignment.title: Build the business case and the safety net
assignment.brief: Calculate saved hours and payback, choose the process, design error handling and monitoring, and write a runbook.

documents.name: Process Data
documents.note: 12 minutes per invoice; 800 invoices a month; automation covers 70%.

documents.name: Error Log
documents.note: Failures from unreadable scans and unknown suppliers.

tasks.title: Hours Saved
tasks.prompt: 12 minutes x 800 invoices x 70% automated. How many hours are saved per month?
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Payback
tasks.prompt: Saved value: 112 h x €25 = €2,800 a month. Build cost €9,000. What is the payback in months?
tasks.reasoning: Payback tells when the investment is recovered.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Process Selection
tasks.prompt: Which process is the best automation candidate?
options: High volume, rule-based, stable and well documented
tasks.mistake: Automating a broken process automates the waste.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Error Handling
tasks.prompt: An unreadable scan arrives. What should the automation do?
options: Route it to a human queue with the reason, never guess
tasks.reasoning: Failures must be visible and recoverable.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Monitoring
tasks.prompt: Select monitoring to put in place.
options: An audit log of every action
Daily count of processed vs rejected invoices
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Runbook
tasks.prompt: Write a 3-5 sentence runbook for the on-call analyst.
tasks.modelAnswer: If the failure rate exceeds 10% in an hour, pause the automation and check the supplier list and scan quality. Send failed invoices to the human exception queue with the error reason and record the incident. Do not reprocess without checking for duplicates. Report the cause and fix to the finance lead the same day.
tasks.reasoning: A good runbook gives thresholds, actions, safeguards and reporting.
tasks.mistake: Retrying without checking duplicates causes double payments.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The Bot That Paid Twice
caseStudy.background: An automation re-ran after a timeout and paid 300 invoices twice. Recovery took two months.
questions: Why did the retry cause duplicates?
caseStudy.solution: Helix added duplicate detection and payment-count alerts.

prompts: Which process in your life would you automate first?
